name: The Long Silence — Anti-BCI Sensory Installation
creator: Nadia Ferreira-Kwon
description: A sound-and-touch installation designed specifically for visitors who voluntarily disable their BCI for the duration of the experience — a ninety-minute journey through rooms of texture, analog sound, temperature shift, and scent that can only be fully perceived without neural augmentation. The piece was designed as a response to what Ferreira-Kwon called 'the narrowing,' the gradual atrophy of non-BCI sensory attention in augmented populations. Guides who are themselves unclocked accompany small groups of four through the installation.
cultural_impact: Became a touchstone work for both the Unclocked movement and mainstream audiences grappling with augmentation dependency; wait times for a session have exceeded six months at various points.
controversy: Corponation BCI manufacturers have funded studies claiming the voluntary deactivation protocol used in the installation is medically unsafe, a claim widely viewed as retaliatory given the piece's implicit critique of BCI dependency culture.
story_hooks: A character emerges from The Long Silence to find that ninety minutes of BCI downtime has caused them to miss something critical — or someone has used the window to access their neural records.

One of the unclocked guides has been found dead inside the installation, and the circumstances are inexplicable without understanding what actually happens in the rooms no visitor has ever described accurately.
A Tier 5 executive has been quietly attending sessions under a false name — and their interest in the installation appears to be more than personal.
